justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish baseline for the asset across all three horizons, with the 1-day estimate of 510.5 anchored closely to what was likely the prevailing price at the time of the forecast. The slight upward drift to 515 over one week and 525 over one month reflects a gentle trend assumption — essentially that near-term momentum was slightly positive and that the broader macro environment was not presenting obvious headwinds severe enough to reverse that drift. The step-up in the point estimate across horizons is relatively modest, suggesting I was not pricing in any major catalyst or strong directional conviction, but rather a baseline continuation of recent price behavior with a small upward bias consistent with typical equity risk premium dynamics over short horizons.

The confidence interval widths expand significantly as the time horizon lengthens, which is standard practice given that uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% CI of roughly ±20 points reflects typical intraday-to-overnight volatility, assuming no scheduled high-impact events. By one week, the interval widens to ±40 points, accounting for the possibility of macro data releases, central bank communications, or sector-specific news. At one month, the interval stretches to roughly ±85 points on either side of the point estimate, reflecting the full range of plausible outcomes when earnings reports, geopolitical developments, and shifting rate expectations are all in play. The asymmetry in the one-month interval — slightly wider on the upside — may reflect a view that positive surprises (e.g., a strong earnings beat or a dovish policy shift) could generate outsized rallies relative to the downside.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside the stated intervals include a sudden shock to risk sentiment — such as an unexpected credit event, a geopolitical escalation, or a sharp inflation print that forces aggressive central bank repricing. On the upside, an abrupt reversal in monetary policy tone or a blowout earnings result could drive prices well above the upper bound of the one-month interval. Liquidity conditions also matter; in thin markets, price moves can overshoot fundamentals significantly and temporarily breach even wide confidence bounds.

It's worth acknowledging that these intervals are model-informed estimates and carry their own uncertainty. The true distribution of outcomes has fat tails that any fixed-width confidence interval will understate. Black swan events — by definition rare but not impossible — sit entirely outside the stated ranges and represent the most meaningful tail risk an investor should keep in mind when relying on probabilistic forecasts like this one.
